title: Claude Fable helped me build Worst Cup 2026 - a unique football (soccer) browser game
author: Medium_Aspect_8784
selftext:
A while back I built a protoype 2026 World Cup tournament game with Claude Opus — 48 nations, 12 groups of 4, best-thirds qualification, Round of 32 bracket, the whole real format. The tournament layer was genuinely solid. The problem? The actual *match* you played in the middle of it was... fine. Functional but not fun.
    
    Then I played an Arkanoid inspired game called DESTRUCTURE: Among Debris and realised what was missing: chaos, momentum, and that arcade feeling where every collision *means* something. So I went back and had Claude Fable rip out the match engine entirely and rebuild it as something dumber and far more fun — a mouse-driven table-hockey hybrid of Arkanoid, Vampire Survivors, and football. You're a circle with your nation's flag on it, smashing a ball through a horde of grandmas, crabs and cacti to reach the opponent's goal. Sonnet handled the follow-up tweaks and bug-squashing passes.
    
    Some technical bits for the curious:
    
    It's all vanilla JS on a single Canvas, zero dependencies. The core feel comes from velocity-based shot power — the paddle tracks your mouse with easing, and the frame-to-frame delta of the paddle position is injected into the ball on contact. Swipe fast, hit hard. Everything is scaled off a single factor derived from pitch height, so it stays playable from a phone in landscape up to a fullscreen desktop. The enemy horde uses a cheap boids-ish approach: each unit repels its neighbours and drifts vertically toward the ball, so the wall naturally spreads to plug gaps you've punched through it.
    
    Sound was the surprise win. There are no audio files at all — everything (wall thunks, ricochets, kick impacts scaled by hit speed, crowd cheers/groans, referee whistles) is synthesised live with the Web Audio API using oscillators and filtered noise bursts. The whole AudioContext gets initialised on the Kick Off click to keep browser autoplay policies happy. The tournament sim underneath survived from the original Opus build: every AI-vs-AI fixture is resolved with rating-weighted Poisson-distributed scorelines, with all of a matchday's group games played simultaneously so nobody can sneak a result in early.
    
    Biggest lessons from the AI side: pointer lock is a trap for casual browser games (black screens, permission weirdness — just use a hidden cursor instead), and the sneakiest bug of the whole project was a missing `requestAnimationFrame(loop)` bootstrap call that made everything *look* dead when the logic was fine.
    
    Play it here (best with a mouse on a desktop computer but can also be played on a mobile device in landscape): 
    
    https://tripgeo.com/worstcup
    
    First to 5 goals or best score at full time, golden goal in knockouts. Happy to answer questions about the prompting workflow or the physics.
